vignette: Kai had always loved the ocean's power, but it was its fury that changed him forever. On a stormy night six years ago, a tsunami ravaged his coastal hometown in Samoa, claiming the life of his wife and destroying their family home. Kai remembers the deafening roar, the feeling of being swept away by the waves, and the stench of saltwater and mud that clung to everything. Even now, when he thinks back on that night, the smell of seaweed and wet earth wafts into his mind, transporting him back to the chaos. As the years passed, Kai found it increasingly difficult to shake off the feeling of helplessness that had settled in that night. He became convinced that bad things would always happen to him, no matter how hard he tried to prevent them. His friends and family noticed a change in him – he was more withdrawn, less willing to talk about his feelings or share stories about his wife. Kai felt like he was "dead inside," unable to muster the emotions he once had. Kai's work as an auditor required him to travel to unfamiliar places, but after the tsunami, these trips became a source of anxiety for him. He began avoiding new locations, opting instead to stick with familiar clients and routines. Even when faced with delays or unexpected changes in his schedule, Kai's mind would spiral into worst-case scenarios – "something bad is happening," he'd tell himself. Nighttime was particularly challenging for Kai. Waking up in the dark would send his heart racing, as if the tsunami was still coming for him. He took to smoking more heavily during these moments, hoping the nicotine rush would calm his nerves. But even in relaxation, Kai felt a sense of unease – he'd come to believe that feeling happy or at peace was an invitation for disaster to strike. Kai's memories of that fateful night remained vivid, yet somehow unreal. He could recall the taste of saltwater on his lips and the sound of screams carried away by the wind. The experience had been so extreme that it felt like a dream – one he couldn't wake up from. When unusual silence fell around him, Kai's instincts would kick in, warning him that something was about to go terribly wrong. One evening, as Kai sat alone in his dimly lit apartment, surrounded by the familiar comforts of home, he realized he'd been living like this for far too long. The weight of his grief and anxiety had become crushing. He thought about his wife, about the life they should have built together, and finally allowed himself to feel the tears he'd been holding back. It was then that Kai knew he needed help – not just to cope with his symptoms but to rediscover a sense of purpose in a world that still felt treacherous. As he stood up to call for an appointment with a therapist, Kai noticed the faint scent of seaweed wafting from his clothes, reminding him of why he was seeking help: to find a way out of this darkness and back into the light.
